regions.name: South Asia
regions.description: A subcontinent of extraordinary musical diversity, home to some of the world's oldest and most sophisticated musical traditions.

regions.name: Middle East
regions.description: A crossroads of musical traditions spanning millennia, with intricate melodic and rhythmic systems.

regions.name: East Asia
regions.description: Musical traditions emphasizing subtlety, breath, and the relationship between sound and silence.

regions.name: Southeast Asia
regions.description: Rich traditions of gamelan, vocal arts, and cross-cultural musical exchange.

regions.name: Africa
regions.description: The birthplace of rhythm, with traditions that have shaped music across the globe.

regions.name: Europe
regions.description: Classical and folk traditions that have influenced music education worldwide.

regions.name: North America
regions.description: A melting pot of traditions that gave birth to jazz, blues, and many popular forms.

regions.name: Latin America
regions.description: Vibrant traditions blending indigenous, African, and European influences.

traditions.name: Hindustani Classical
traditions.description: One of the world's most sophisticated melodic traditions, Hindustani classical music centers on raga (melodic framework) and tala (rhythmic cycle). Performances often begin with slow, contemplative improvisation and build to rhythmic complexity.
characteristics: Extensive use of microtonal ornamentation (meend, gamak)
Gradual build from slow alap to fast gat

terminology.definition: A melodic framework defining specific notes, phrases, and emotional character
A rhythmic cycle with a specific number of beats and internal groupings
A musical note; the basic building block of melody
Slow, unmetered improvisation introducing the raga
A composed melody with rhythmic accompaniment
A smooth glide between notes

traditions.name: Carnatic Classical
traditions.description: The classical music tradition of South India, Carnatic music is known for its intricate compositions, complex rhythmic patterns, and systematic approach to melody through the melakarta raga system.
characteristics: Integration of singing with violin accompaniment

terminology.definition: A system of 72 parent ragas covering all possible 7-note scales
A composed piece with lyrics, typically in three sections
Improvisational exploration of a raga without rhythmic accompaniment
Improvisation on the lyrics of a composition at a specific point
The primary percussion instrument, a double-headed drum

traditions.name: Arabic Maqam
traditions.description: Arabic maqam music is built on a system of melodic modes (maqamat) that use quarter tones and intricate intervallic relationships. The tradition emphasizes modal improvisation (taqsim) and complex rhythmic patterns (iqa).
characteristics: Maqam modal system with quarter tones

terminology.definition: A melodic mode with specific intervals, characteristic phrases, and emotional quality
A free-rhythm improvisation exploring a maqam
A rhythmic cycle pattern played on percussion
A fretless lute, central to Arabic music
An interval approximately half a semitone, characteristic of Arabic tuning

traditions.name: Persian Classical
traditions.description: Persian classical music (dastgah system) features intricate melodic modes, elaborate ornamentation, and a poetic tradition deeply intertwined with music. Performances follow a structured improvisational framework.

terminology.definition: A modal system comprising a hierarchy of melodic units (gusheh)
The complete repertoire of melodic models that forms the basis of learning
Free-rhythm improvisation within a dastgah
A vocal ornament involving rapid alternation between registers
A melodic model or section within a dastgah

traditions.name: Japanese Traditional
traditions.description: Japanese traditional music emphasizes the beauty of silence, subtle pitch variations, and the concept of 'ma' (space between sounds). Traditions range from court music (gagaku) to intimate solo instrumental pieces.
characteristics: Connection to tea ceremony, martial arts, and Zen

terminology.definition: The meaningful space or pause between sounds
An end-blown bamboo flute used in meditation and music
A 13-string zither, one of Japan's most iconic instruments
Ancient court music, one of the oldest orchestral traditions
A structural concept of gradual acceleration

traditions.name: Chinese Traditional
traditions.description: One of the world's oldest continuous musical traditions, Chinese music is deeply connected to philosophy, medicine, and the natural world. The pentatonic scale forms the foundation of most Chinese music.
characteristics: Connection to Confucian and Daoist philosophy
Association with five elements and seasons

terminology.definition: The first and most important note of the pentatonic scale
A two-stringed bowed instrument with a expressive, voice-like tone
A four-stringed plucked lute with a bright, percussive sound
A seven-stringed zither associated with scholars and contemplation
The beat or rhythmic accent in Chinese music

traditions.name: West African Rhythmic
traditions.country_or_area: West Africa (Ghana, Mali, Senegal, Guinea, Nigeria)
traditions.description: West African musical traditions are characterized by complex polyrhythmic structures, call-and-response patterns, and the centrality of drums in community life. These traditions have influenced music worldwide.
characteristics: Music as communal and social function

terminology.definition: The simultaneous use of two or more conflicting rhythmic patterns
A goblet-shaped hand drum capable of a wide range of sounds
A traditional storyteller, historian, and musician
A repeating rhythmic pattern that serves as the foundation for ensemble playing
A 21-string bridge-harp combining features of lute and harp

traditions.name: Celtic Traditions
traditions.description: Celtic music encompasses the folk traditions of the Celtic nations, featuring distinctive ornamentation, dance rhythms, and a strong oral tradition. The music ranges from lively dance tunes to haunting airs.

terminology.definition: A lively dance tune in 4/4 time with even subdivision
A dance tune in 6/8 time with characteristic long-short rhythm
An Irish frame drum played with a tipper
Old-style unaccompanied singing with elaborate ornamentation
Informal gathering of musicians playing traditional tunes together

traditions.name: Flamenco
traditions.description: Flamenco is a passionate and complex art form combining singing (cante), dance (baile), and guitar (toque). It draws from Romani, Moorish, Jewish, and Spanish folk traditions.
characteristics: Interplay between singer, dancer, and guitarist

terminology.definition: The rhythmic cycle that forms the foundation of each palo
The heightened state of emotion and expression in performance
A style or form within flamenco with specific rhythm and mood
Deep song, the most serious and emotional form of flamenco singing
A guitar technique using rapid finger strumming

traditions.name: Latin American
traditions.description: Latin American music represents a rich fusion of indigenous, African, and European traditions. From Brazilian samba to Argentine tango, these traditions emphasize rhythm, dance, and communal celebration.

terminology.definition: A five-note rhythmic pattern that serves as the foundation of Afro-Cuban music
A Brazilian dance and music style with African rhythmic roots
An Argentine dance form characterized by dramatic pauses and sharp movements
A Cuban musical genre combining Spanish and African elements
Tall, narrow drums central to Latin American and Caribbean music

traditions.name: Jazz
traditions.description: Jazz emerged from the convergence of African rhythmic traditions, blues, and European harmony. It is characterized by improvisation, swing feel, and a tradition of individual expression within ensemble playing.

terminology.definition: A rhythmic feel where eighth notes are played with a long-short pattern
A style emphasizing fast tempos, complex harmonies, and virtuosic improvisation
Accompaniment played by piano or guitar behind a soloist
A bass line playing steady quarter notes, outlining the harmony
The chord progression of a jazz standard

traditions.name: Western Classical
traditions.description: Western classical music encompasses a vast tradition of composed music spanning from medieval chant to contemporary works. It developed systems of harmony, counterpoint, and notation that influenced music education globally.

terminology.definition: A musical form with exposition, development, and recapitulation
The art of combining independent melodic lines
The variation of loudness in music (piano, forte, etc.)
The quality or color of a musical sound
A harmonic progression that provides a sense of resolution

instruments.name: Sitar
instruments.description: A long-necked plucked string instrument with movable frets and sympathetic strings, producing a distinctive resonant sound.

instruments.name: Tabla
instruments.description: A pair of hand drums (dayan and bayan) capable of a remarkable range of tones and pitches.

instruments.name: Oud
instruments.description: A fretless, short-necked lute with a deep, warm tone. Central to Arabic and Middle Eastern music.

instruments.name: Shakuhachi
instruments.description: An end-blown bamboo flute with a haunting, breathy tone. Used in meditation and musical performance.

instruments.name: Koto
instruments.description: A 13-string zither with movable bridges. Japan's most iconic traditional instrument.

instruments.name: Erhu
instruments.description: A two-stringed bowed instrument with a voice-like quality. Often called the 'Chinese violin'.

instruments.name: Pipa
instruments.description: A four-stringed plucked lute with a bright, percussive sound and rapid tremolo technique.

instruments.name: Djembe
instruments.description: A goblet-shaped hand drum capable of bass, tone, and slap sounds. Originating from West Africa.

instruments.name: Kora
instruments.description: A 21-string bridge-harp combining features of lute and harp. Central to griot tradition.

instruments.name: Tin Whistle
instruments.description: A simple six-holed wind instrument with a bright, clear tone. Essential to Irish traditional music.

instruments.name: Uilleann Pipes
instruments.description: Irish bellows-blown bagpipes with a complex, sweet tone and wide range.

instruments.name: Bodhran
instruments.description: An Irish frame drum played with a double-headed stick (tipper).

instruments.name: Flamenco Guitar
instruments.description: A nylon-string guitar played with distinctive rasgueado (strumming) and picado (picking) techniques.

instruments.name: Cajón
instruments.description: A box-shaped percussion instrument played by slapping the front face.

instruments.name: Congas
instruments.description: Tall, narrow single-headed drums played with hands. Central to Afro-Cuban music.

instruments.name: Bandoneon
instruments.description: A concertina-like instrument essential to Argentine tango music.

instruments.name: Saxophone
instruments.description: A single-reed woodwind instrument with a rich, expressive tone. Iconic in jazz music.

instruments.name: Piano
instruments.description: A keyboard instrument capable of melody, harmony, and rhythm simultaneously.

instruments.name: Violin
instruments.description: A four-stringed bowed instrument with a wide range and expressive capabilities.

instruments.name: Veena
instruments.description: A plucked string instrument with a deep, resonant tone. Central to Carnatic music.

instruments.name: Mridangam
instruments.description: A double-headed barrel drum providing rhythmic foundation in Carnatic music.

instruments.name: Tar
instruments.description: A long-necked waisted lute with a skin-covered soundbox. Central to Persian classical music.

instruments.name: Ney
instruments.description: An end-blown flute with a breathy, soulful tone. One of the oldest instruments still in use.

instruments.name: Balafon
instruments.description: A wooden xylophone with gourd resonators. Used in West African orchestras.

instruments.name: Mbira
instruments.description: A thumb piano with metal tines mounted on a wooden board. Used in Shona music of Zimbabwe.

scales_modes.name: Raga Yaman
scales_modes.description: An evening raga with a raised fourth degree. Royal and luminous in character.

scales_modes.name: Raga Bhairav
scales_modes.description: A morning raga with flattened second and sixth degrees. Deeply devotional.

scales_modes.name: Raga Kafi
scales_modes.description: A versatile raga used in light classical and folk music.

scales_modes.name: Raga Bhoopali
scales_modes.description: A pentatonic evening raga. Joyful and bright.

scales_modes.name: Thaat System
scales_modes.description: A system of 12 parent scales from which ragas are derived.

scales_modes.name: Melakarta System
scales_modes.description: A systematic classification of 72 parent ragas covering all possible 7-note scales.

scales_modes.name: Maqam Rast
scales_modes.description: The most important maqam in Arabic music. Contains characteristic quarter tones.

scales_modes.name: Maqam Hijaz
scales_modes.description: A widely recognized mode with an augmented second interval.

scales_modes.name: Maqam Bayati
scales_modes.description: One of the most common maqamat, with a characteristic quarter tone on the second degree.

scales_modes.name: Maqam Kurd
scales_modes.description: A mode similar to the Western Phrygian, common in Kurdish and Arabic music.

scales_modes.name: Dastgah-e Shur
scales_modes.description: The most common dastgah, the 'mother of Persian music'.

scales_modes.name: In Scale (Minor Pentatonic)
scales_modes.description: A traditional Japanese scale with a minor character. Used in folk and court music.

scales_modes.name: Yo Scale
scales_modes.description: A bright, open scale used in folk music and festivals.

scales_modes.name: Pentatonic (Gong)
scales_modes.description: The most common Chinese pentatonic scale, associated with the earth element.

scales_modes.name: Mixolydian Mode
scales_modes.description: A major scale with a lowered seventh degree. Common in Celtic and folk music.

scales_modes.name: Dorian Mode
scales_modes.description: A minor scale with a raised sixth degree. Used in Celtic, jazz, and folk traditions.

scales_modes.name: Phrygian Mode
scales_modes.description: A mode with a characteristic half-step between the first and second degrees. Core of flamenco.

scales_modes.name: Blues Scale
scales_modes.description: A scale featuring the 'blue note' (flattened fifth). Foundation of blues and jazz.

scales_modes.name: Major Scale
scales_modes.description: The foundational scale of Western music theory.

scales_modes.name: Natural Minor Scale
scales_modes.description: The relative minor of the major scale. Foundation of minor key harmony.

rhythms.name: Teentaal
rhythms.description: The most common tala in Hindustani music. 16 beats divided into 4 groups of 4.

rhythms.name: Jhaptaal
rhythms.description: An asymmetric tala with 10 beats divided into 5 groups of 2.

rhythms.name: Rupak Tala
rhythms.description: A 7-beat tala with an unusual first group of 3 beats.

rhythms.name: Adi Tala
rhythms.description: The most common tala in Carnatic music. 8 beats divided into 4 groups of 2.

rhythms.name: Maqsum
rhythms.description: A common Arabic rhythmic pattern used in popular and classical music.

rhythms.name: Samai
rhythms.description: A rhythmic pattern used in formal Arabic instrumental music.

rhythms.name: West African Polyrhythm
rhythms.description: Layered rhythmic patterns combining 3 against 4, creating complex textures.

rhythms.name: Bell Pattern (Standard)
rhythms.description: The standard bell pattern that serves as timeline for West African ensembles.

rhythms.name: Jig Rhythm
rhythms.description: A compound meter pattern (6/8) characteristic of Irish jigs.

rhythms.name: Reel Rhythm
rhythms.description: A simple meter pattern (4/4) with even subdivision, used in Irish reels.

rhythms.name: Bulería Compás
rhythms.description: A fast, complex 12-beat cycle used in the most virtuosic flamenco style.

rhythms.name: Soleá Compás
rhythms.description: A slow, solemn 12-beat cycle. The 'mother of flamenco' palos.

rhythms.name: Son Clave
rhythms.description: The fundamental rhythmic pattern of Afro-Cuban music (3-2 or 2-3).

rhythms.name: Bossa Nova Rhythm
rhythms.description: A syncopated guitar pattern characteristic of Brazilian bossa nova.

rhythms.name: Swing Feel
rhythms.description: The characteristic long-short eighth note feel of jazz.

rhythms.name: Walking Bass
rhythms.description: Steady quarter-note bass line outlining harmony, foundation of jazz rhythm section.
